lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice giving a simple scheduling update with correct V2 word order after time expressions.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Two adults coordinate a weekday plan after a small change in timing.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Updating someone about when something will happen.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik discuss a changed meeting time and confirm what works today.

main_focus.name: main-clause inversion after time expressions
main_focus.description: When a time expression starts the sentence, the verb comes before the subject in the main clause.
model_examples: I dag börjar mötet klockan fyra.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use this word order naturally 3-4 times in the dialogue.

allowed_supporting_grammar: basic questions with när and vilken tid

useful_chunks: I dag hinner jag inte tidigare.
vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use most active words if they fit naturally, with repeated exposure to time phrases.

dialogue_shape.opening: One person gives a short update about a changed time.
dialogue_shape.middle: They check availability, mention one reason for the change, and suggest a workable time.
dialogue_shape.ending: They confirm the final time and what happens next.

target_complexity.repetition: some natural repetition of fronted time expressions is useful

focus: the final time that is agreed

sentence_focus: one sentence starting with i dag plus V2 word order
one sentence starting with efter jobbet plus kan
one sentence asking what time something starts
one sentence saying a time does not work
one sentence confirming the new plan
